bank_title: NEONATAL / INFANT CRANIAL ULTRASOUND — PHRASES BANK

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Prematurity screening (31 weeks GA, Day 7 of life).

subs.title: Findings
items: Sonographic evaluation through the anterior fontanelle demonstrates normal midline structures and age-appropriate sulcation.
The lateral, third, and fourth ventricles are normal in size and configuration (AHW: 1.5 mm bilaterally).
The caudothalamic grooves are unremarkable with no evidence of germinal matrix or intraventricular hemorrhage.
Periventricular white matter shows normal echogenicity without focal lesions or cystic change.
Posterior fossa structures including the cerebellar hemispheres and vermis are normal.
Anterior cerebral artery Resistive Index is normal at 0.72.

subs.title: Impression
items: Normal neonatal cranial ultrasound for gestational age. No evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, ventriculomegaly, or periventricular leukomalacia.

bank.title: 2. Germinal Matrix / Intraventricular Hemorrhage (GMH-IVH - Papile Grades)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Extreme prematurity (26 weeks GA), acute drop in hematocrit.

subs.title: Findings
items: Right Side: Large, well-defined hyperechoic mass centered in the right caudothalamic groove extending into the body and occipital horn of the right lateral ventricle, occupying greater than 50% of the ventricular lumen and causing acute ventricular dilatation (AHW: 8.5 mm). No periventricular hemorrhagic venous infarction identified.
Left Side: Small focal hyperechoic clot confined to the left caudothalamic groove without intraventricular extension or ventricular dilatation (AHW: 2.0 mm).
Midline shift of 3 mm to the left is noted.

subs.title: Impression
items: Right-sided Grade III intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) with acute post-hemorrhagic ventriculomegaly and mild leftward midline shift.
Left-sided Grade I germinal matrix hemorrhage (GMH).
Serial follow-up cranial ultrasound recommended in 3 to 5 days to monitor ventricular size.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: 29 weeks GA premature infant, Day 28 follow-up scan.

subs.title: Findings
items: Compared to the baseline scan, there is interval development of multiple discrete, well-defined anechoic cysts within the bilateral frontoparietal periventricular white matter (superolateral to the external angles of the lateral ventricles), measuring up to 4 mm in diameter.
Mild ex-vacuo dilatation of the bilateral lateral ventricles is present (AHW: 4.5 mm bilaterally).
No acute hemorrhage is seen.

subs.title: Impression
items: Bilateral cystic periventricular leukomalacia (Grade III PVL) with mild secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly. Correlate with neurodevelopmental follow-up and brain MRI at term-equivalent age.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Term neonate (39 weeks GA), perinatal asphyxia, low Apgar scores.

subs.title: Findings
items: Gray-scale imaging demonstrates diffuse, symmetric increased echogenicity throughout the cerebral cortex and subcortical white matter, resulting in loss of normal gray-white matter differentiation ("bright brain" appearance).
Effacement of the cortical sulci and slit-like compression of the lateral ventricles are noted consistent with diffuse cerebral edema.
Increased echogenicity is also present in the bilateral thalami and basal ganglia.
Spectral Doppler of the anterior cerebral artery demonstrates marked luxury perfusion with elevated end-diastolic velocities and a markedly decreased Resistive Index (RI = 0.45).

subs.title: Impression
items: Diffuse cerebral edema with deep gray nuclei involvement and markedly reduced cerebral vascular resistance (RI = 0.45), consistent with severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). Urgent clinical correlation advised.

bank.title: 5. Benign Enlargement of Subarachnoid Spaces (BESS / External Hydrocephalus)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: 6-month-old infant with rapidly crossing head circumference percentiles (macrocephaly) and normal neurological exam.

subs.title: Findings
items: There is prominent widening of the frontal subarachnoid spaces (sinocortical width = 7.5 mm; craniocortical width = 8.0 mm) and widening of the anterior interhemispheric fissure (7.0 mm).
Multiple normal cortical veins are clearly visualized traversing the fluid spaces up to the inner table of the calvarium ("cortical vein sign"), ruling out subdural hygroma.
The lateral, third, and fourth ventricles are normal in size (AHW: 2.5 mm).
Parenchymal echogenicity is normal.

subs.title: Impression
items: Benign enlargement of the subarachnoid spaces of infancy (BESS), evidenced by widened frontal extra-axial fluid spaces with preserved traversing cortical veins and normal ventricular caliber. No subdural collection.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: 3-week-old neonate with fever, irritability, and bulging fontanelle.

subs.title: Findings
items: Echogenic, thickened ependymal lining is noted along the bilateral lateral ventricles.
Coarse, mobile echogenic debris and low-level internal echoes are layering within the occipital horns of both lateral ventricles, accompanied by early ventriculomegaly (AHW: 6.0 mm).
Echogenic widening of the sulci with increased leptomeningeal color Doppler hyperemia is also identified.

subs.title: Impression
items: Findings consistent with acute bacterial meningitis complicated by ventriculitis and early communicating hydrocephalus. Urgent clinical and CSF correlation required.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Term newborn presenting with high-output congestive heart failure and cranial bruit.

subs.title: Findings
items: Midsagittal and coronal views demonstrate a large, well-circumscribed midline anechoic cystic structure located posterior to the third ventricle in the region of the quadrigeminal cistern, measuring 2.4 x 2.1 cm.

Color and spectral Doppler interrogation reveals turbulent, high-velocity, low-resistance arterialized venous flow within the lesion with multiple tortuous feeding arteries, causing secondary obstructive hydrocephalus of the lateral and third ventricles.

subs.title: Impression
items: Vein of Galen aneurysmal malformation (VOGM) with secondary obstructive hydrocephalus. Urgent neurointerventional and pediatric cardiology consultation recommended.
